title: Bonami Fourth Moment Inequality
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$. For a uniformly random sign vector $X\in\{-1,1\}^n$, its moments satisfy $\mathbb E[f(X)^4]\le 9^k\bigl(\mathbb E[f(X)^2]\bigr)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on the n-dimensional sign cube
The Fourier degree of f is at most k
